correctness.rationale: The exact equivalence between universal cycles and connected balanced Eulerian edge sets (at least five retained edges) is proved directly. The 32-variable GF(2) incidence kernel is exhaustively enumerated using its rank-15 matrix; integer balance filters 6600 of 131072 candidates. A second 2^16+2^16 divergence-signature enumeration independently yields exactly the same 6600 balances and 33 exact valid counts, using a disjoint-set connectivity checker instead of breadth-first search. Two self-contained files were run from actual delivery source paths; exhaustive finite work suffices because the claim fixes order five.

originality.rationale: Full-text primary comparison: Chen–Kitaev–Sun, arXiv:1908.01116 / Mathematics 8 (2020) 778, Tables 1–3 exhaust the binary cases through order four; Theorem 6 gives two-deletion values for arbitrary order; Theorem 5 states a lower bound at order at least five, not the full 33-coefficient order-five existence distribution. Their lower bound at five deleted words counts four sets, whereas the exact connected-Eulerian enumeration here finds fourteen. Public research-record semantic searches and the accessible original records did not identify a stronger published count. This is not proof against obscure or unpublished equivalent tabulations.

value.rationale: The 2020 paper supplied full binary probability tables for n<=4 and only general lower bounds at n>=5. Determining all 33 fifth-order deletion probabilities is the first missing full binary order, not an arbitrary sample. The gap at five deleted words (bound four versus exact fourteen) shows that known lower-bound construction does not already exhaust the problem; the complete table quantifies when degree balance ceases to imply a connected universal cycle, yielding natural reusable finite benchmark data.
